title: Connect your tools
content:
## What you'll get

You'll learn how to plug external services—like Google Sheets, Slack, and Stripe—into your Emergent app so it can send emails, store data, or accept payments without writing integration code yourself.

---

## Think of integrations as power outlets

An integration is like plugging your app into a power outlet for a specific service. Emergent has built-in "sockets" for a curated set of tools—databases, payment processors, email senders, messaging apps—so you don't have to build those connections from scratch.

When you connect an integration, you give your app permission to talk to that service on your behalf. For example:

- **SendGrid** – your app can send transactional emails (password resets, order confirmations).
- **Stripe** – your app can accept credit card payments and manage subscriptions.
- **Google Sheets** – your app can read or write spreadsheet data in real time.
- **Slack** – your app can post messages to channels or send notifications.
- **MongoDB** – a managed database is automatically provisioned for every workspace to store your app's data.

<Callout type="info" title="Screenshot coming soon">
Screenshot of the integrations catalog will go here.
</Callout>

All API keys and credentials are encrypted and never exposed in logs or your app's code—Emergent injects them securely at runtime.

---

## A few useful integrations

Here are some of the most common integrations beginners use, grouped by what they help you do:

**Send messages or emails:**
- **SendGrid** – transactional email delivery (e.g., welcome emails, receipts).
- **Twilio** – SMS, voice calls, and WhatsApp messages.
- **Slack** – post updates to a Slack workspace.

**Accept payments:**
- **Stripe** – process credit cards, manage subscriptions, handle billing.

**Store files or data:**
- **MongoDB** – a NoSQL database that's automatically set up for every workspace (no configuration needed).
- **AWS S3** – object storage for images, videos, and documents.
- **Google Sheets** – read and write spreadsheet data.

**Track usage and errors:**
- **Google Analytics** – track page views and user events.
- **Sentry** – monitor errors and performance issues.

<Callout type="tip" title="Start simple">
If you're building your first app, start with MongoDB (already included) and one messaging or payment integration. You can add more later.
</Callout>

---

## How to ask the agent to connect a tool

You don't need to configure integrations manually—just describe what you want in chat and the agent will guide you.

<Steps>
<Step title="Describe the task in plain English">
For example:

- *"I need to send an email when someone signs up."*
- *"Let users pay with Stripe."*
- *"Pull data from this Google Sheet every hour."*
</Step>

<Step title="The agent will ask for credentials">
If the integration requires an API key or secret (most do), the agent will prompt you to provide it. You'll add these values in your workspace settings under **Integrations** or **Environment Variables**.
</Step>

<Step title="The agent writes the code">
Once you've added the credentials, the agent generates the integration code—connecting to the service, calling the right endpoints, and handling errors.
</Step>
</Steps>

<Callout type="note" title="Where to find API keys">
Most services provide API keys in their developer or settings dashboard. The agent will tell you exactly where to look for each service (e.g., "Get your SendGrid API key from Settings → API Keys").
</Callout>

<Callout type="info" title="Video coming soon">
A short screen recording showing how to ask the agent to connect Stripe will go here.
</Callout>

---

## If you're not sure which integration to use

If you know *what* you want to do but not *which* service to use, just ask the agent:

- *"How do I send emails from my app?"* → The agent will suggest SendGrid or another email provider.
- *"I need to accept payments."* → The agent will recommend Stripe or PayPal and explain the difference.
- *"Where should I store user profiles?"* → The agent will suggest MongoDB (already included) or another database.

The agent knows which integrations are available on Emergent and will guide you to the right one.

---

## Advanced: custom integrations with MCP

<Callout type="warning" title="Draft - needs review">
This section (advanced MCP connector setup for custom tools not in the catalog) needs product confirmation before publishing.
</Callout>

If you need to connect a service that isn't in the catalog, Emergent supports the **Model Context Protocol (MCP)**—an open standard that lets the agent discover and use external tools dynamically. You can register custom MCP servers in your workspace settings to give the agent access to proprietary APIs, internal databases, or third-party tools.

For most beginners, the built-in catalog will cover your needs. If you're curious about MCP, see the advanced docs once you've built your first app.
